set.approach: From the Fairy Meadow base camp take the usual path through Friendship Col onto the glacier. Bear right past Sentinel's south ridge, to the col between East Peak and Pioneer, then climb the steep snow slope up the north-northeast ridge to the first prominent rock step.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: Gibraltar rises along the glacier's southern margin. From the Fairy Meadow base camp take the usual path through Friendship Col onto the glacier. The route starts at the obvious splitter hand crack, reached by stepping across the moat from a snow bank; check the moat edge before stepping, since the snow there can be undercut.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route. A long double-rope rappel from just below the mantle corner can reach the first pitch station, or it can be broken into shorter rappels.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: Ironman is the conspicuous buttress closing the upper Austerity Glacier. Access to the Adamants is usually by helicopter, or on foot from Fairy Meadow over Friendship Col and Thor Pass to the Adamant Glacier. The original start is now hard to reach as the ice has shrunk, so begin in the middle of the buttress and follow a ramp and ledge system to the highest belay on the right side, then traverse around the corner to the first crack.
set.descent_text: Walk north to the end of the plateau and go down westward by a loose gully system onto the upper Austerity Glacier, starting from fixed slings. An ice axe and crampons are strongly recommended, because the gully drops onto the steep upper headwall of the glacier.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: Access to the Adamants is usually by helicopter, or on foot from Fairy Meadow over Friendship Col and Thor Pass to the Adamant Glacier. From the Austerity Glacier reach the col between Adamant and Blackfriars, then head directly up the South Buttress.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route, since fixed tat marks every belay, or hike down from the summit on its west side and circle back to the Austerity Glacier.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: Access to the Adamants is usually by helicopter, or on foot from Fairy Meadow over Friendship Col and Thor Pass to the Adamant Glacier. The route climbs the Horn's big buttress. Begin up the large gash or chimney on the right side of the toe of the lower buttress and climb it to a large vegetated ledge, which is the true start.
set.descent_text: Descend east with short rappels, or from a camp in the Horn and Unicorn basin traverse north over the Unicorn and along the divide separating the Horn basin from the Granite Glacier basin to the saddle, then descend west to the low point of a snowfield above a cliff band. Rappels and scrambling down the slabby cliff band lead back to the upper Horn basin.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the Mud Creek parking lot, walk the trail between two large square boulders, then up the well-built trail that leaves the gravel stream bed, taking the left fork. The trail passes the base of Small Walls and reaches the signed base of Ahren's Rock. The route is a slender crack just right of a large flake, partway down the rock from the Morning Glory area.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the Goat Lake Main logging road, stay right at the Dianne branch junction and left at the D-branch junction (a four-wheel-drive road), then cross the bridge over the river. The flagged trail leaves on the right soon after the bridge, climbs through old-growth forest along the southwest ridge, crosses a large gully, and reaches Camp Radagast and then the foot of the wall. Then walk along the foot of the cliff to the start; the line is clear once you are below it.
set.descent_text: Descend by rappelling On the Virg; carry two ropes and extra slings.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the Goat Lake Main logging road, take the D-branch road to the flagged trail that climbs through old-growth forest to Camp Radagast and the foot of Amon Rudh. The line sits at the far western end of the cliff; expect to thrash uphill before crossing the gully by the camp.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the Applebee Dome camp, scramble east and down to find the large boulder, which is only moments away. A wide crack splits its south wall and angles upward from right to left; that crack is the route.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: Park at the BC Hydro campground at Seton Lake, cross the aqueduct and walk to the base of the wall. The route starts to the right of The Weremouse and climbs the buttress on the right side of the gully that the Weremouse's alternate start follows on its left.
set.descent_text: The descent is the same as The Weremouse: head toward Lillooet and follow goat and bighorn trails downhill to the one break in the cliff band above the highway.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: Park at the BC Hydro campground at Seton Lake, cross the aqueduct and walk to the base of the wall. The route is on the left-hand side of the face.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: Park at the BC Hydro campground at Seton Lake, cross the aqueduct and walk to the base of the wall. The approach to this route is longer than to the others because it climbs talus to reach the base. It is the right-most route on the face and begins on a big pale slab beneath a yellow roof.
set.descent_text: Head toward Lillooet and follow goat and bighorn trails downhill; the cliff band above the highway has a single break, which the goat trail leads to. The descent comes out east of the aqueduct.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the overgrown clearcut low on the Rexford trail, head up and left to a forested ramp and follow it, on fourth class ground, to the base of the Chinese Puzzle Wall low on the west ridge of South Illusion Peak. The route takes the central line up the wall, beginning in the central crack system.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the overgrown clearcut low on the Rexford trail, head up and left to a forested ramp and follow it, on fourth class ground, to the base of the Chinese Puzzle Wall low on the west ridge of South Illusion Peak. The climbing begins by traversing left across a loose, vegetated ledge to a ledge with a big tree.
set.descent_text: Descend by way of Hidden Dragon.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: Follow the Sky Pilot approach to the Stadium Glacier and traverse west toward Copilot. Seppuku is on the north side of the peak, to the right of the main chimney that splits the face on the viewer's left; the first pitch climbs a right-arcing crack and slot that begins with a small roof.
set.descent_text: Rappel the NE route from bolted anchors.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: Follow the normal Sky Pilot approach up to the Stadium Glacier, then cross easy snow slopes west to the foot of Copilot. Leave the snow and scramble up to the start of a corner, which is where the climbing begins; the scree can be extensive late in summer.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the Applebee Dome camp, go left and up from the campground and head for the foot of the wall, following faint paths through boulders and past what is left of the Crescent Glacier. The route climbs the middle of the south face of the Donkey Ears. One start climbs two cracks that meet in a triangle; the other traverses in from the left along the approach ledge, past the point where the wall turns black with lichen.
set.descent_text: The route ends in the notch between the two ears, with the summit of the east ear reached by cracks and ledges on its north side. From the top of the east ear rappel steeply east, then scramble north and east to the eastern slopes of the Crescent Towers, staying high. Work down to the col with Eastpost Spire and hike down to Applebee Dome.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the Applebee Dome camp, go left and up from the campground toward the base of the large formation under the Donkey Ears, following vague paths through the boulders. The route is on the South Tower, up the steep white wall beside and right of Thatcher Cracker, starting at the lowest point of the south face, on a short white wall under a large roof.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the Applebee Dome camp, go left and up from the campground to the base of the formation. Eeyore starts where Ears Between does and then bears right: take the fourth class ramp or the harder direct start to a ledge, with the Ears up and to the left and Eeyore up and to the right.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the Applebee Dome camp, take the path below the campground and follow the branch that climbs up and left toward the big formation with the Donkey Ears showing above it. The route starts at the extreme left end of the foot of the Central Towers, just uphill from a big pale flake leaning on the cliff, and heads up and right through fourth and low fifth class ground.
set.descent_text: Go down the gully that separates the North Tower from the Central Towers. Rappel anchors are there to get past the steepest section, and an axe is useful if the gully still holds snow.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the Applebee Dome camp, go left and up from the campground toward the base of the formation. The route starts in the main weakness between Lion's Way and Tiger's Trail, on fourth class ground, and later joins Lion's Way below its easy fifth class section.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the Applebee Dome camp, go left and up from the campground toward the base of the Crescent Towers. The direct start is on the south face, below and a little left of a black boulder that sits at the top of the first pitch, which puts it nearly under the left Donkey Ear.
set.descent_text: Bolted anchors at the top of the south summit allow a rappel to the north side.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the Applebee Dome camp, go left and up from the campground and stay high past the base of the Donkey Ears. The route follows the vague buttress to the right of Lion's Way and to the left of the first Donkey Ear's steep wall, with an extra opening pitch starting from a grassy ledge.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the parking area at the northwest corner of Crest Lake, cross the highway and follow the trail east to the Crow's Nest. Look for the prominent arete; the route starts in a corner a couple of metres to its left.
